why: Live in CI (ship-gate.yml:202), fully offline, meeting the house CI rule now. Targets use a bespoke argparse `selftest`, not pytest (0 test_*.py exist outside vendored .venv), so mutmut/cosmic-ray's core model -- mutate + rerun an existing pytest suite -- needs a layer never adopted here. These specs narrate WHY each mutation matters, tied to 2 real regressions this harness already found in bus.py, and grade each catch as named-check/crash/survived (mutate.py:172-194), not bare pass/fail. For 5 small files read by one person, that outweighs generic auto-coverage.

alternatives.name: mutmut
alternatives.covers: Automatic AST mutation generation (operator/constant/some statement swaps) across a module, re-running the project's existing pytest suite per mutant, with caching + survived/killed dashboard.
alternatives.gap: Assumes a pytest suite; this repo has none (0 test_*.py outside vendored .venv). Gives pass/fail per mutant only, not the named-[FAIL]/crash/survived 3-way diagnosis mutate.py prints.
alternatives.cost: Free/OSS; adds pytest+mutmut as new dependencies to a repo with zero test-framework dependency today.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained, v3.3.1 latest per search; one of the most-used Python mutation tools.

alternatives.name: cosmic-ray
alternatives.covers: Same generic AST-mutation-vs-existing-tests model as mutmut; config-driven (TOML), distributed/parallel mutant execution, pluggable operators.
alternatives.gap: Same pytest-suite assumption gap; same loss of the named-check/weak-signal diagnostic; multi-line domain-specific regressions here still need hand-authoring anyway.
alternatives.cost: Free/OSS; adds its own SQLite work-db/config layer as new machinery for 5 small files.
alternatives.maturity: Actively maintained -- release dated 2026-04-02 per search; supports Python 3.9-3.13.

alternatives.name: mutatest
alternatives.covers: Lightweight AST mutation testing against an existing pytest suite (or configurable command); random-sample mode for speed.
alternatives.gap: Same pytest-suite assumption; search could not confirm current maintenance cadence either way (treated as unverified, not dead).
alternatives.maturity: Unclear from this search whether actively maintained; not independently confirmed.

alternatives.name: pytest-mutagen
alternatives.covers: Decorator-based (@mutagen.mutant) mutations written beside the function they mutate -- closer in spirit to this repo's hand-authored style than a blind AST sweep.
alternatives.gap: Confirmed inactive: no PyPI release in the past 12 months per search; still a pytest plugin, so inherits the same pytest-suite dependency gap.
alternatives.cost: Free/OSS, but adopting a stalled dependency is itself a cost.
alternatives.maturity: Inactive/discontinued (confirmed by search: no PyPI release in past 12 months).

alternatives.name: universalmutator
alternatives.covers: Language-agnostic regex mutation tool that runs an ARBITRARY shell command as the kill-oracle -- structurally the closest match to mutate.py's own 'run the target's selftest' model.
alternatives.gap: Mutation rules are generic per-language regex operators, not per-behavior; no concept of this repo's specific named regressions or which check caught them.
alternatives.maturity: Research-oriented; current activity level not confirmed by this search.

evidence: Read all 6 spec files in full + mutate.py:1-252. CI-wired: ship-gate.yml:202-203 runs `mutate.py --spec all`. Confirmed 0 test_*.py outside vendored .venv; selftest subcommands at bus.py:849, refute.py:492, snap.py:818, run.py:355/572, plain.py:623. WebSearched mutmut/cosmic-ray/mutatest/pytest-mutagen/universalmutator maintenance.
recheck: python tools/audit/mutate.py --spec all (expect exit 0, 'every mutation ... applied and ... caught'); grep -n mutate.py .github/workflows/ship-gate.yml; check mutmut/cosmic-ray PyPI release dates for continued maintenance.
migration_loc: 0 recommended now. Full migration to mutmut/cosmic-ray: ~+40 ln (pytest shim/target) but loses the named-check/weak-signal diagnostic and regression narration; not attempted.
what_ours_does: 5 hand-authored specs (bus.py 112/plain.py 168/refute.py 80/skilleval.py 138/snap.py 193 ln) each list named (behavior, meaning, exact find-string, replace-string) mutations against ONE real tool file. tools/audit/mutate.py(252 ln, outside the counted 702) substitutes each into a sibling copy, runs the target's own `selftest`, and reports caught/survived/weak-signal per mutation.
strongest_counterargument: mutmut(v3.3.1)/cosmic-ray(released 2026-04-02) are actively maintained, generate mutations by AST not brittle exact-string `find` (a rename here silently desyncs a spec, caught only later as SKIP), and a 5-line pytest shim per target's `selftest` would let either own the ~40 generic boundary/constant/operator-flip entries, shrinking hand-authored surface roughly in half.
